dedupe_keys.name: network rtk disrupted by travelling ionospheric disturbances in china during the 1 june 2025 geomagnetic storm

description: This paper gives observational evidence that a geomagnetic storm degraded network real-time kinematic (NRTK) positioning in low-latitude China. The storm of 1 June 2025 generated large-scale travelling ionospheric disturbances over China, seen by dense GNSS networks, with amplitudes of plus or minus 0.4 TECU, equatorward speeds of 0.3 to 1.3 km/s and wavelengths of 1,150 to 1,600 km during the main phase. These gradients broke the spatial correlation assumed by NRTK interpolation, giving residuals above 10 cm, largest for satellites south of the user station, so integer ambiguity resolution often failed and horizontal accuracy fell to the 5 to 10 cm level. Producer: eight authors publishing in the journal Space Weather, dated 1 June 2026. Coverage: dense GNSS networks over low-latitude China during one storm. Access: open access; the abstract and licence were taken from the OpenAlex record because the publisher page was blocked. Licence and cost: CC BY-NC-ND per OpenAlex, free to read. Caveats: a single event, and the reference network data were not read here. Simulation uses: it quantifies a vulnerability pathway from geomagnetic activity to decimetre-level errors for precision positioning services in hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the Gannon storm GNSS degradation and agriculture loss case (case_study-gannon-storm-gnss-agriculture-losses-2024).
